notes: Curated CIK/ticker identity evidence for the 30-control universe. Every record must cite a checkable primary source, and no CIK may be written from recollection. Statuses follow the approved evidence hierarchy: MANUAL_VERIFIED requires a human-checked filing citation; RESOLVED is reached by sec_company_tickers or filing_document_text; name matching and full-text search can never establish a mapping on their own. Absence of evidence is recorded as absence. Dated lifecycle facts are scope-tagged and kept out of valid_from/valid_to, which mean generic ticker validity and are a broader claim than any single filing supports. Verified so far: AAPL, GM (both issuers), IPET. Run `tradeit edgar verify-control <ID> --index-root <DIR>` to gather candidates for the rest.

controls.notes: The easy case, and the pilot's baseline. One issuer, continuously listed, currently trading, so the SEC's own company_tickers.json is authoritative for the CURRENT CIK-to-ticker relationship. Recorded as RESOLVED rather than MANUAL_VERIFIED: sec_company_tickers is sufficient primary SEC evidence under the approved ranking, while MANUAL_VERIFIED stays reserved for a human-checked filing citation. valid_from and valid_to are deliberately null — the ticker file proves the mapping as of its retrieval date and says nothing about which historical dates AAPL was valid, and the filing spine corroborates issuer continuity without dating the ticker.

controls.notes: The hard case, and it resolved without an identity break. Pets.com, Inc. became IPET Holdings, Inc. by charter amendment on 2001-01-16 -- one issuer, one CIK, one continuous registrant. The rename is a lifecycle fact rather than a second issuer mapping, and the model already refuses the wrong representation: two mappings sharing a CIK is a ConfigError, and a second mapping would force identity_break true. The 2000 prospectus gave the symbol; the 2002 10-K gave what it could not -- the dates the security actually traded under IPET, and that it continued afterwards under IPETZ, which is preserved in scope_notes because no date for it is established. The 2005 Form 15-12G names a different company in its signature block; every competing primary field identifies IPET Holdings, so the anomaly is recorded on the fact it affects rather than allowed to alter identity. The lesson worth keeping: for a pre-2001 delisted issuer the ticker is recoverable from the offering document, but the dates it was valid come from a later periodic report.

valid_from and valid_to describe THE LIFE OF THE TICKER 'IPET' ONLY.

valid_from = 2000-02-11 and valid_to = 2001-01-18 rest on symbol-specific filing-body evidence, not on the delisting event: SEC Form 10-K filed 2002-03-29, IPET Holdings, Inc., CIK 1100683, accession 0000891618-02-001559, Item 5 states "From February 11, 2000, the date of our initial public offering, to January 18, 2001, the date of our Nasdaq Stock Market delisting, our common stock was traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the symbol IPET." The 2000-02-11 prospectus proved only that the symbol was approved for quotation, which is a different claim; the 10-K is what establishes the dates the security actually traded under this symbol.

These dates are NOT issuer existence: the issuer continued after 2001-01-18 to wind up, liquidate, settle liabilities and distribute, and kept filing with the SEC until 2005. They are NOT security-class extinction: the same class continued to be quoted over the counter under a different symbol.

TICKER TRANSITION, UNDATED. The same 10-K, Item 5, states "The closing price of our common stock on January 18, 2001 was $0.125. Our stock has subsequently continued to trade under the symbol IPETZ through over-the-counter quotation services, such as Pink Sheets..." The exact start and end dates of that OTC quotation are NOT established by any document consulted, and none is derived from the delisting date -- 2001-01-18 is when Nasdaq quotation ended, not when OTC quotation began. IPETZ is therefore recorded here in prose rather than as a dated lifecycle fact, is deliberately NOT written into this mapping's ticker field, and is NOT represented as a second issuer mapping: a successor quotation symbol for the same class of the same issuer is not a second identity. It is also NOT scoped exchange_listing anywhere in this record, because OTC quotation services quote rather than list and there is no listing agreement, listing standard or delisting process to cite.

lifecycle_facts.fact: Operational wind-down. On 2000-11-04 the Board resolved that if no viable acquisition or financing offer was received by 9:00 a.m. on 2000-11-07, the Company would begin the orderly wind down of its operations, lay off approximately 255 of its 320 employees, and undertake efforts to sell the majority of its assets including inventory, distribution-center equipment, URLs, content and intellectual property. The filing states that no viable offers had been received by 9:00 a.m. on 2000-11-07.
lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 8-K filed 2000-11-07, Pets.com, Inc., CIK 1100683, accession 0001095811-00-004383 (local copy petscom-2000-11-07-8k.txt); the attached press release is headed "Pets.com (Nasdaq: IPET)"
lifecycle_facts.note: This is an OPERATIONAL fact about the issuer and nothing more. It is NOT a legal dissolution date, NOT a bankruptcy date, NOT an exchange delisting date, NOT a security extinguishment date, and NOT a ticker valid_to. A company that begins winding down operations continues to exist legally, may keep filing, and its securities may keep trading for some period afterwards. Each of those would need its own filing to establish, and none has been consulted.

lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 8-K filed 2001-01-17, Pets.com, Inc., CIK 1100683, accession 0000891618-01-000054: "On January 16, 2001, the stockholders of the Company approved the Plan of Complete Liquidation and Dissolution of the Company and the change of corporate name from Pets.com, Inc. to IPET Holdings, Inc." The same filing states that an amendment to the Certificate of Incorporation effecting the name change was filed on January 16, 2001.

METADATA DISCREPANCY PRESERVED: the SGML header carries DATE OF NAME CHANGE 19991208, which conflicts with the filing-body chronology establishing the Pets.com, Inc. -> IPET Holdings, Inc. name change in January 2001. lifecycle_facts.fact: A Certificate of Dissolution was filed on 2001-01-16 and took effect on 2001-01-18.
lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 8-K filed 2001-01-17, Pets.com, Inc., CIK 1100683, accession 0000891618-01-000054, which states the Certificate of Dissolution was filed on January 16, 2001 and that "The Certificate of Dissolution will take effect on Thursday, January 18, 2001." Retrospectively corroborated by SEC Form 10-K filed 2002-03-29, IPET Holdings, Inc., CIK 1100683, accession 0000891618-02-001559.
lifecycle_facts.note: THIS IS NOT CORPORATE EXTINCTION. Under Delaware law a dissolved corporation continues to exist for the purpose of winding up. The issuer continued after this date to wind up its affairs, liquidate assets, settle liabilities and make distributions to stockholders, and continued to file with the SEC until 2005. Nothing in the record establishes a date on which the entity ceased to exist, and none may be inferred from this fact. The 8-K states the effective date prospectively; the 10-K is later evidence that it occurred, and the two are recorded as one fact with two citations rather than as two events.

lifecycle_facts.fact: The Common Stock was delisted from the Nasdaq Stock Market on 2001-01-18.
lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 8-K filed 2001-01-17, Pets.com, Inc., CIK 1100683, accession 0000891618-01-000054, which states that at the close of business on January 18, 2001 the Common Stock would be delisted from the Nasdaq Stock Market. Nasdaq was not a registered national securities exchange until 2006; this issuer registered under Section 12(g) (Form 8-A12G), and Rule 12d2-2 / Form 25 applies to exchange-listed securities. The 8-K and 10-K are the primary evidence, not a fallback. Removal from listing ends a listing and nothing else: the same 10-K states the security continued to be quoted over the counter afterwards.

lifecycle_facts.fact: Form 15-12G filed 2005-06-03 certifying termination of registration of the Common class under Section 12(g), Commission File No. 000-29387, with approximately 251 holders of record. The form relies expressly on Rule 12g-4(a)(1)(i), the fewer-than-300-holders route.
lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 15-12G, IPET HOLDINGS INC, CIK 1100683, accession 0000950134-05-011306; EDGAR header FILED AS OF DATE 20050603
lifecycle_facts.note:
The relied-upon rule is established from the raw HTML, not inferred from context: the Rule 12g-4(a)(1)(i) box is Wingdings ý (checked ballot box) while every visible alternative is Wingdings ¨ (empty box). This is primary evidence of the Section 12(g) registration-termination route applicable to fewer than 300 holders of record.

DATES ARE KEPT SEPARATE AND NONE IS TREATED AS THE LEGAL TERMINATION DATE. Filing date = 2005-06-03 (EDGAR header FILED AS OF DATE 20050603). SOURCE-DOCUMENT ANOMALY, RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED: the signature block of this document reads "Beyond.com Corporation has caused this certification/notice to be signed...". Each issuer carries its own CIK and evidence, and identity_break is true so the merge cannot happen by accident. Note the asymmetry the two records preserve: old GM's ISSUER lifecycle continued through bankruptcy and liquidation long after its EXCHANGE LISTING ended, so those two scopes close at different times and are recorded separately. Neither issuer carries a valid_from or valid_to: the evidence establishes CIK-to-ticker relationships and one dated exchange-listing removal, and none of it dates generic ticker validity at either end.

controls.notes:
One continuing registrant across a merger, a d/b/a and a ticker change. The GTE transaction was a REVERSE TRIANGULAR merger: Bell Atlantic's wholly owned subsidiary Beta Gamma Corporation merged with and into GTE, leaving GTE a subsidiary of Bell Atlantic. The registrant itself merged into nothing, survived as the parent, and kept CIK 732712 -- which is why identity_break is false and why this control is the deliberate contrast to GM, where two genuinely different registrants shared a ticker.

Two filings carry the control. A 1999 filing states the NYSE symbol BEL outright and maps it to CIK 732712; the 2000-06-30 8-K establishes the merger direction and the transition to VZ. Both symbols are therefore evidenced and neither is inferred.

The existing schema expressed this without change. A ticker-interval structure was proposed conditionally before the evidence arrived; it is not needed, because the VZ transition carries a DATE and therefore fits LifecycleFact, which the undated IPETZ transition did not.

mappings.citation: TICKER: SEC filing under CIK 732712, accession 0000950130-99-002148, manually inspected, which states three times that the symbol is BEL: "Bell Atlantic shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol 'BEL'."; in the comparative market price section, "GTE common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol 'GTE'. Bell Atlantic common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol 'BEL'."; and "The Bell Atlantic ticker symbol on the New York Stock Exchange is 'BEL'."  --  ISSUER CONTINUITY AND THE LATER SYMBOL: SEC Form 8-K filed 2000-06-30, Bell Atlantic Corporation, CIK 732712, accession 0000950134-00-005461, manually inspected. That filing states that on June 30, 2000 Bell Atlantic Corporation and GTE consummated their merger; that Beta Gamma Corporation, a New York corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Bell Atlantic, was merged with and into GTE so that GTE became a wholly owned subsidiary of Bell Atlantic; and that Bell Atlantic common stock would be listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol VZ. Its attached press release states that Verizon Communications would begin trading on the NYSE under the new symbol VZ on Monday, July 3, 2000.
mappings.scope_notes:
One issuer, CIK 732712, continuous across the GTE merger. The registrant was the acquiring parent in a reverse triangular merger and did not itself merge into anything; GTE became its subsidiary. No second issuer exists for this control and identity_break is false.

TICKER 'BEL' IS ESTABLISHED BY PRIMARY EVIDENCE. SEC filing under CIK 732712, accession 0000950130-99-002148 states the NYSE symbol outright, three times, including once in a comparative market price section that names GTE's symbol alongside it. An earlier draft of this record carried 'VZ' in this field and recorded the historical symbol as an open gap, because no filing then inspected named it; that gap is closed and the field now holds the symbol the control is keyed on.

THE LATER SYMBOL 'VZ' IS A DATED LIFECYCLE FACT, NOT A SECOND MAPPING. A symbol change on a continuing issuer is not an identity break, and a second mapping would be doubly wrong: two mappings sharing CIK 732712 is a load error, and any second mapping would force identity_break true. The transition is instead an exchange_listing fact dated 2000-07-03. That works here and did not work for IPET's successor symbol IPETZ for one reason: VZ has a date and IPETZ has none. This is why no schema change was needed.

valid_from IS NULL. The 1999 filing states a STATE -- the shares 'are listed' under the symbol BEL -- not the date that listing began. Bell Atlantic's own first day under BEL is not established by anything inspected.

valid_to IS NULL. No filing establishes BEL's last trading session. The press release is prospective about VZ beginning on Monday 2000-07-03; deriving the preceding Friday from a trading calendar would be arithmetic, not evidence. The symbol transition is dated where it belongs, in the exchange_listing fact. This follows the IPET precedent: a prospective statement about a symbol does not become generic ticker validity, and IPET's own valid_from moved off null only when a later filing stated retrospectively that the stock had traded from a given date.

NO LEGAL NAME-CHANGE EFFECTIVE DATE IS RECORDED. The bylaws attached to the 8-K, marked amended effective as of 2000-06-30, identify the registrant as 'BELL ATLANTIC CORPORATION (Doing Business As Verizon Communications)'. A d/b/a is not a legal name change, and no date for a legal change is inferred from it or from the later EDGAR index and header showing VERIZON COMMUNICATIONS INC with a former name of BELL ATLANTIC CORP.

lifecycle_facts.fact: Merger consummated on 2000-06-30. Beta Gamma Corporation, a New York corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Bell Atlantic Corporation, was merged with and into GTE, and as a result GTE became a wholly owned subsidiary of Bell Atlantic. Bell Atlantic Corporation, CIK 732712, remained the continuing parent issuer.
lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 8-K filed 2000-06-30, Bell Atlantic Corporation, CIK 732712, accession 0000950134-00-005461
lifecycle_facts.note: REVERSE TRIANGULAR MERGER, AND THE DIRECTION MATTERS. The disappearing entity was Bell Atlantic's own subsidiary, not Bell Atlantic; GTE survived as a subsidiary. The registrant is therefore continuous and this is NOT an identity break, NOT a successor issuer and NOT a security extinguishment. Contrast GM, where two different registrants with two different CIKs shared one ticker -- there the break is real and declared.

lifecycle_facts.fact: In the merger, GTE common shares were converted into the right to receive Bell Atlantic common shares, and Bell Atlantic would issue approximately 1.175 billion Bell Atlantic common shares in the transaction.
lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 8-K filed 2000-06-30, Bell Atlantic Corporation, CIK 732712, accession 0000950134-00-005461
lifecycle_facts.note: This is an ISSUANCE into the existing common class, not the creation of a new class and not the extinguishment of the old one. The security a holder of Bell Atlantic common owned before the merger is the same security afterwards, in a larger share count. The class whose shares were extinguished was GTE's, and GTE is a different registrant that is not part of this control.

lifecycle_facts.fact: Bell Atlantic common stock was to be listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol VZ, and trading under that new symbol was to begin on Monday, 2000-07-03.
lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 8-K filed 2000-06-30, Bell Atlantic Corporation, CIK 732712, accession 0000950134-00-005461: the filing states Bell Atlantic common stock would be listed on the NYSE under the symbol VZ, and the attached press release of the same date states that Verizon Communications would begin trading on the NYSE under the new symbol VZ on Monday, July 3, 2000.
lifecycle_facts.note:
THIS DATE IS NOT THE MERGER DATE. The merger was consummated 2000-06-30; trading under VZ began 2000-07-03. They are three days and one weekend apart and they are different events -- collapsing them would place the symbol change on a day no filing supports.

PROSPECTIVE STATEMENT. The press release says trading 'would begin' on that Monday. No retrospective confirmation has been inspected, which is why this date is recorded here rather than as ticker valid_from.

THE PRIOR SYMBOL IS NAMED ELSEWHERE, NOT HERE. This 8-K calls VZ a 'new symbol' without saying what it replaced. The predecessor symbol BEL is established separately by SEC filing under CIK 732712, accession 0000950130-99-002148 and is carried in this mapping's ticker field.

Unlike IPET's 2001 Nasdaq delisting, exchange_listing is unambiguously the right scope here: the New York Stock Exchange was a registered national securities exchange throughout.

lifecycle_facts.fact: Bylaws attached to the 8-K and marked amended effective as of 2000-06-30 identify the registrant as "BELL ATLANTIC CORPORATION (Doing Business As Verizon Communications)".
lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 8-K filed 2000-06-30, Bell Atlantic Corporation, CIK 732712, accession 0000950134-00-005461, attached amended bylaws
lifecycle_facts.note:
A D/B/A IS NOT A LEGAL NAME CHANGE, and this record does not claim one. What is evidenced is that as of 2000-06-30 the registrant was doing business as Verizon Communications while its stated corporate name was still Bell Atlantic Corporation. No legal corporate-name-change effective date is recorded anywhere in this record.

METADATA, KEPT AS METADATA: a later filing under the same CIK 732712 is indexed as VERIZON COMMUNICATIONS INC and identifies BELL ATLANTIC CORP as the former company. That is EDGAR reflecting a name, and the IPET pilot established that such header values can conflict with the filing-body chronology outright. It is not used as a legal effective date and the contemporaneous 8-K governs.

controls.notes:
THE NEGATIVE CONTROL, AND IT PASSED. Every ingredient of a false exit is present here: an operating business that restructured hard in 2000, a Nasdaq delisting in April 2001, a move to the OTC bulletin board, and a 598-day gap in periodic filings between 2003-09-23 and 2005-05-13. None of it is an exit, and the methodology does not make one.

What the record does NOT contain is the finding. There is no Form 15 of any kind and no Form 25 anywhere in 360 indexed filings; periodic reporting resumed after the gap and runs to 2026-05-22 under the same registrant name, THEGLOBE COM INC, unchanged since 1998-07-24. Nothing establishes dissolution, deregistration, security extinguishment or an issuer replacement, so nothing of the sort is recorded.

The absence of a Form 25 is expected rather than surprising: Nasdaq was not a registered national securities exchange until 2006, so Rule 12d2-2 did not reach this delisting. The event is evidenced by the registrant's own 10-Q instead, which is why it is a dated fact rather than a gap.

mappings.citation: TICKER, NASDAQ ERA: SEC Form 10-K for fiscal 2000, filed 2001-04-02, theglobe.com, inc., CIK 1066684, accession 0000950130-01-001623, manually inspected: "Our common stock is quoted on the NASDAQ National Market under the Symbol 'TGLO'."  --  TICKER, OTC ERA, AND THE DELISTING: SEC Form 10-Q filed 2001-05-15, theglobe.com, inc., CIK 1066684, accession 0000950130-01-501712, manually inspected: "On April 23, 2001, following appeal by the Company to the Nasdaq Listing Qualifications Panel with respect to the delisting of its common stock from the Nasdaq National Market, the Company was delisted from the Nasdaq national market due to its non-compliance of the Company's common shares with the required $1 bid price. Accordingly, the Company was required to move the listing of its common stock from the Nasdaq national market to the Over-the-Counter (\"OTC\") market on what is commonly referred to as the OTC bulletin board, where it is traded under the symbol TGLO."
mappings.scope_notes:
One issuer, CIK 1066684, continuous from 1998 to the present. The indexed registrant name is THEGLOBE COM INC across the entire local span, 1998-07-24 through 2026-05-22, with no variant.

THE SYMBOL DID NOT CHANGE WHEN THE VENUE DID. The FY2000 10-K names the symbol on Nasdaq as TGLO; the 2001-05-15 10-Q names it on the OTC bulletin board as TGLO. The form 'TGLO.OB' appears in later filings and is the OTCBB venue notation appended to the base symbol -- it is not a second security, not a second issuer, and not a ticker in its own right. No second mapping exists and none is warranted: a change of quotation venue is not a change of identity.

valid_from IS NULL. Nothing inspected establishes when TGLO quotation began. The FY2000 10-K states that the stock 'is quoted' under the symbol, which is a state and not a start date; the 1998 offering document, which would date it, has not been inspected.

valid_to IS NULL, AND THE DELISTING DOES NOT SUPPLY ONE. The 2001-04-23 delisting ended a Nasdaq listing, not the symbol: the same 10-Q sentence that reports the delisting states the stock trades under TGLO on the OTC bulletin board afterwards. Lifecycle-event dates and ticker-validity boundaries are kept distinct, and no boundary is inferred from an event that the evidence shows did not end the symbol.

OPERATING RESTRUCTURING, RECORDED HERE AND NOT AS A DATED FACT. Per SEC Form 10-K for fiscal 2000, filed 2001-04-02, theglobe.com, inc., CIK 1066684, accession 0000950130-01-001623, the registrant recorded $41.3 million of restructuring and impairment charges, shut down its Seattle e-commerce operations, and terminated or reduced employees. No filing inspected assigns a day to any of that -- the charges are a fiscal-year aggregate -- so it is preserved here with its citation rather than given a manufactured date. It is a business event and nothing more: NOT a complete business shutdown, NOT shell status, NOT dissolution, NOT deregistration, NOT security extinguishment, NOT an identity break. A named business line closing is not the company closing.

THE OTC TRANSITION IS UNDATED. The 10-Q reports the move to the OTC bulletin board as a consequence of the delisting but gives no date for the first OTC quotation, and 2001-04-23 is not borrowed for it: that is the day the Nasdaq listing ended, which is a different event from the day OTC quotation began.

SEC-REPORTING CONTINUITY IS EVIDENCE, NOT A LIFECYCLE EVENT. 360 indexed filings, 55 Forms 10-K and 77 Forms 10-Q, run to 2026-05-22. The 598-day gap between 2003-09-23 and 2005-05-13 is an INTERIOR gap: filings resumed and continue, so it is not cessation and cannot become one. No sec_reporting fact is recorded, because continuing to file is the absence of an event.

lifecycle_facts.fact: On 2001-04-23, following the Company's appeal to the Nasdaq Listing Qualifications Panel, the common stock was delisted from the Nasdaq National Market for non-compliance with the required $1 bid price. The stock thereafter traded on the OTC bulletin board under the symbol TGLO.
lifecycle_facts.citation: SEC Form 10-Q filed 2001-05-15, theglobe.com, inc., CIK 1066684, accession 0000950130-01-501712: "On April 23, 2001, following appeal by the Company to the Nasdaq Listing Qualifications Panel with respect to the delisting of its common stock from the Nasdaq National Market, the Company was delisted from the Nasdaq national market due to its non-compliance of the Company's common shares with the required $1 bid price. Accordingly, the Company was required to move the listing of its common stock from the Nasdaq national market to the Over-the-Counter (\"OTC\") market on what is commonly referred to as the OTC bulletin board, where it is traded under the symbol TGLO."
lifecycle_facts.note:
A VENUE EVENT AND NOTHING MORE. This is NOT issuer extinction, NOT bankruptcy, NOT registration termination, NOT security-class extinguishment, and NOT a survivorship exit. The same sentence that reports the delisting reports the stock still trading, under the same symbol, on another venue -- so the security plainly survived the event that removed it from Nasdaq.

NO FORM 25 EXISTS AND NONE SHOULD BE SOUGHT. Nasdaq was not a registered national securities exchange until 2006, so Rule 12d2-2 and Form 25 did not apply to this delisting. Its absence from the index is the expected result, not a coverage gap, and the registrant's own 10-Q is the primary evidence rather than a fallback.

THE DATE IS THE DAY THE LISTING ENDED. The Nasdaq determination of non-compliance and the Company's appeal both precede it -- the FY2000 10-K, filed 2001-04-02, still described the stock as quoted on Nasdaq with an appeal pending -- and the 2001-05-15 filing date of the report is later. Determination date, appeal date, filing date and delisting date are four different things and only the last is recorded here.

The OTC move is deliberately left undated. It is a consequence stated in the same sentence, not an event the filing dates, and 2001-04-23 is not borrowed for it.
